RoomType.rationale: QueenBoss declares RoomType.Boss; bucket membership agrees (queen only in boss_keys).

Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: QueenBoss.cs declares Slots => ["amalgam", "queen"] (a real, non-empty row), but QUEEN_BOSS (queen.py) is constructed as `Encounter(id="queen_boss", monster_classes=[TorchHeadAmalgam, Queen])` with no `slots=` argument, so it inherits the Encounter dataclass default `()`. Proposed shared mechanism id encounter/_slot_order (see rationale for why this is a shared shape, not unique to Queen). Filed as a gap on the Slots hook because the sim's Encounter dataclass DOES support a non-empty slots row (Fabricator/Ovicopter use it, per monster/fabricator.json's guard closing this exact mechanism there in round 7) -- QueenBoss is simply not wired to it, even though its own C# clearly declares one.

CustomBgm.rationale: Presentation only: an FMOD event path. No sim counterpart; no observable gameplay effect.

HasCustomBackground.rationale: Presentation only, same reasoning as encounter/test_subject: the background rng it consumes is a dedicated background-asset stream (NCombatRoom.GenerateBackgroundRngForCurrentPoint), never the run's or the encounter's Rng, so no draw is skipped that parity needs. No sim background rendering exists at all.

HasScene.rationale: Presentation only: gates whether a Godot scene is instantiated for this encounter's combat UI. No sim counterpart; no observable gameplay effect.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: C#'s AllPossibleMonsters array literal is [Queen, TorchHeadAmalgam] (Queen first); the sim's monster_classes is [TorchHeadAmalgam, Queen] (amalgam first). AllPossibleMonsters is an unordered superset used for previews/asset-preload, not a placement list, so the two sides agreeing as a SET is the right bar (order divergence here carries no consequence, unlike the GenerateMonsters tuple order, which is verdicted separately). Both models exist and both are always-spawning, fixed members -- no possible set divergence.

ExtraAssetPaths.rationale: Presentation only: preloads the 'Bound' affliction's card-overlay art (ModelDb.Affliction<Bound>().OverlayPath) so it doesn't pop in mid-fight. This is an asset-preload path string only; the Bound affliction's actual mechanical application (via Queen's ChainsOfBindingPower move) is a power-tier concern, not this encounter's, and is not duplicated here per rule 3.

GetCameraScaling.rationale: Presentation only: a camera zoom-out factor (0.9) for this 2-monster boss fight's framing. No sim camera/rendering layer exists.

GetCameraOffset.rationale: Presentation only: a fixed downward camera pan (Vector2.Down * 60). No sim camera/rendering layer exists.

GenerateMonsters.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Roster and ORDER are faithful (see rationale), but the slot-tag half of each C# tuple is dropped: QueenBoss.cs's GenerateMonsters returns (TorchHeadAmalgam, "amalgam") then (Queen, "queen"), while the sim's create_monsters (via the default Encounter.create_monsters, since QUEEN_BOSS supplies no monster_slots) zips monster_classes against an empty monster_slots tuple, so `zip()` yields nothing and neither creature's slot_name is ever set -- both stay None instead of 'amalgam'/'queen'. Same mechanism as, and filed jointly with, the Slots hook above (encounter/_slot_order); see that entry's rationale for the full dormancy witness and the cross-record note about monster/fabricator.json's guard.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: Same structural fact as every unit in this batch.

guards.rationale: sts2_rl/rewards.py GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.BOSS] = (100, 100) and QUEEN_BOSS sets neither min_gold nor max_gold -- matches. Poverty/ascension scaling out of scope per PROMPT.md.
QueenBoss does not override ShouldGiveRewards; Encounter.should_give_rewards defaults True and is left unset here -- matches.
